Enviromental Ed Day 1 I Know Nothing Except The Fact Of My Ignorance

Sep 9, 2010 • Janice Cotcher

This coming year is terribly exciting for me. I only have 6 classes over 2 semesters and then I’m done! Probably more exciting than the prospect of being done is everything I’ll learn this year. I’m comfortable with scientific concepts but not with teaching them. My biggest frustration in life is I want to be an expert before I’ve really begun. Although my ignorance vexes me, I am thankful for the opportunities ahead.

Today in class, the instructor said something that triggered the question in my mind “How can I incorporate environmental education into the physics curriculum?” The thought of my task ahead scares me a little bit. Classes like biology seem to be naturally suited to environmental education but there has to be a way. I have a couple ideas so far of concepts that I might be able to use

  • thermodynamics
  • Conservation of Energy
  • Kepler’s Laws of planetary motion
  • Newton’s Laws (how the push and pull of forces changes our landscape) Physics means the study of the physical laws of the universe so surely there must be many ways to incorporate nature.

Environmental education is not a required class for me but I felt like I need to take it. I see such beauty in physics, mathematics and nature but I just need to find a way to show it to others. I think of a former student who once told me that it was all my fault that she sees math everywhere she looks and she can’t turn it off. Good, I’ve done my job.
